request: If the model cannot solve stress tests, try to fix it while preserving failures and criteria.
numerical_scope: Repeat the exact 65 full-stack interventions in transformer_stress/plan.json for each declared fix. Retain FP32 parameters and residual states. Widen only vulnerable internal calculations. Compare every result to the original v1 failure and an independent FP64 reference of the intended original equations. These are finite-grid accuracy fixes, not a theorem of global finite-precision stability.
range_rms: Maximum-scaled RMS forward in FP64, cast back to the input dtype; same epsilon and real function. Pairwise wedge FP64 backward avoids a large projection subtraction in radial directions. This correctness prototype has quadratic width cost with a chunked temporary; runtime is not a selection criterion.
wide_rotary: Build the intended warped angle and exp(log_frequency) in FP64 before sin/cos; cast the tables to FP32 for the original attention. Same learned parameters and positional function. No unannounced clamp or frequency bound. Very large FP64 angles remain sensitive; values beyond FP64 range are outside this declared stress grid.
wide_swiglu: Compute input projections, SiLU/value products and output projection through Peri-RMS in FP64, then return FP32. Keep matrices, post-RMS coefficient and functional equation unchanged.
wide_xsa: Keep original FP32 QKV projections, Q/K normalization, scores, probabilities and cached values. Compute the centered clipped XSA projection and output projection through output RMS in FP64. No change to clipping epsilon or cache semantics.
all_numeric_bounded_rope: Separately declared mathematical change on top of all numerical fixes: effective log frequency is 4*tanh(raw_log_frequency/4). Its multiplier lies between exp(-4) and exp(4), derivative magnitude <= exp(4), and initial value/derivative match the unbounded alpha=0 parent. Very large raw values can saturate its gradient. This prevents exp(alpha) and its derivative from growing without bound; it changes the model and is compared to its own explicitly bounded FP64 equation. All original stress interventions and parameters are retained. Wider angle calculations alone cannot keep an arbitrarily large frequency gradient representable in an FP32 parameter.
learning_scope: Repeat all 84 v1 residual cells with only SwiGLU changed from SiLU(gate)*value to (1+SiLU(gate))*value. This adds a linear path using the same matrices, without new parameters. Keep the original epsilon, residual choices, data, teacher strengths, seeds, sampler, LR, optimizer, 512-update budget, 5% relative-MSE threshold and ranking. Initial weights match but initial outputs intentionally change. Do not mix numerical fixes into this learning ablation.
learning_motivation: All 84 v1 learning cells missed the 5% threshold despite finite optimization. A train-only linear least-squares diagnostic gets held-out relative MSE 0.06226956, so a linear path alone is not sufficient; the nonlinear part still must learn. The proposed change is not an oracle feature or a threshold relaxation.
selection: Numerical fixes are judged by full-grid finite outputs/gradients and errors versus the intended equations, including ordinary controls and all originally failed cases. Learning uses the unchanged v1 ranking and retains all cells. No early99 source changes or new long-data tuning. Freeze source hashes before scientific execution.
